```{r}

rm(list = ls())

## Load packages and dataset Note in this script the file paths are set up for my own laptop, you will need to update all the filepaths to point at your own repository or drive

# Install required packages if not already installed
required_packages <- c("tidyverse", "grf", "data.table", "skimr", "janitor", "missForest", "ggplot2", "pROC","purrr","dplyr","tibble", "broom", "forcats","foreign","httr","jsonlite","terra","randomForest","readxl","stringr","sf","ranger","caret")
installed <- installed.packages()
to_install <- setdiff(required_packages, rownames(installed))
if (length(to_install) > 0) install.packages(to_install)

# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(grf)         # Honest causal forests
library(data.table)  # Fast data handling
library(skimr)       # For quick descriptive stats
library(janitor) # Clean column names
library(missForest) #handling NAs
library(ggplot2)
library(pROC)
library(purrr)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(broom)
library(forcats)
library(foreign)
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(terra)
library(randomForest)
library(readxl)
library(stringr)
library(sf)
library(ranger)
library(caret)


#training data from LISS panel 
new_vars <- fread("/Users/jeroen/Downloads/Datasegmentation for Jeroen/output.csv") %>% clean_names()

df_model_unique<- read_excel("/Users/jeroen/Downloads/Datasegmentation for Jeroen/data_long_4c.xls")

# Recalculate hosehold members based on partner and children
df_model_unique <- df_model_unique %>%
  mutate(
    members = 1 + partner + children
  )

#  Sanity check  

df_model_unique %>%
  select(partner, children, members) %>%
  head(10)

#  Handle categorical/ordered variables
df_model_unique <- df_model_unique %>%
  mutate(
    educat = factor(educat, levels = 1:6, ordered = TRUE),
    urban = urban + 1,
    urban = factor(urban, levels = 1:5, ordered = TRUE),
    occupation = as.factor(occupation),
    year_built = as.factor(year_built),
    rental = as.factor(rental),          # just to be safe
    partner = as.factor(partner),
    children = as.integer(children),
    female = as.factor(female)           # 1 = female, 0 = not
  )

# Quick check
summary(df_model_unique$educat)
summary(df_model_unique$urban)

merged_df <- merge(df_model_unique,new_vars,by = "nomem_encr",all.x = TRUE)

merged_df <- merged_df %>%
  mutate(
    nettohh_z = scale(nettohh)[, 1] # Convert to numeric vector from matrix
  )

#Class 1 - Financially driven (12.9%)
#Class 2 - Policy driven (17.3%)
#Class 3 - Erratic choosers (13.1%)
#Class 4 - Comfort driven (56.7%)

class_weights <- c(
  Class1 = 1 / 0.129,
  Class2 = 1 / 0.173,
  Class3 = 1 / 0.131,
  Class4 = 1 / 0.567
)

# Define dataset for random forest training 
rf_training <- merged_df %>%
  select(
    nomem_encr,
    class_4class,          # ✅ target
    female,                # matched by female_share
    age,                   # matched by avg_age
    members,               # matched by huishoudgrootte
    year_built,            # from LISS, matched to avg_build_year or BAG
    rental,                # matched by rental_share
    urban,                 # already available
    nettohh_z,             # matched by income_z
    square_meters          # matched by oppervlakte_m2
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(class_4class))  # drop rows with missing class label
# Prepare data: remove ID columns and factor target
rf_for_impute <- rf_training %>%
  select(-nomem_encr) %>%
  mutate(class_4class = as.factor(class_4class))

# Run missForest helps flesh out any missing data 
set.seed(123)
rf_imputed_result <- missForest(rf_for_impute)

# Extract the completed data
rf_training_imputed <- rf_imputed_result$ximp

rf_imputed_result$OOBerror

```

```{r}
#Random forest training 
# If not already done:
rf_data <- rf_training_imputed %>%
  mutate(class_4class = as.factor(class_4class))  # ensure factor target

rf_data$class_4class <- factor(rf_data$class_4class,
                               levels = 1:4,
                               labels = c("Class1", "Class2", "Class3", "Class4"))

# Set up 10-fold CV
set.seed(123)
cv_control <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 10,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  savePredictions = "final"
)
# Define hyperparameter grid
rf_grid <- expand.grid(
  mtry = (2:8),
  splitrule = c("gini", "extratrees"),
  min.node.size = c(1, 3, 5, 10, 20)
)
# Train random forest with CV
cv_model <- train(
  class_4class ~ ., 
  data = rf_data,
  method = "ranger",
  trControl = cv_control,
  importance = "permutation",
  tuneGrid = rf_grid,
  num.trees = 1000,  # stable without overkill
  class.weights = class_weights
)

# View performance
print(cv_model)
plot(cv_model)


final_rf_model <- ranger(
  class_4class ~ .,
  data = rf_data,
  importance = "permutation",
  mtry = cv_model$bestTune$mtry,
  splitrule = cv_model$bestTune$splitrule,
  min.node.size = cv_model$bestTune$min.node.size,
  num.trees = 1000,
  seed = 123,
  class.weights = class_weights
)
print(final_rf_model)
```

```{r}
# Preview the data
str(cbs_pc6)

process_cbs6_data <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(across(
      .cols = -postcode_6,
      .fns = ~ as.numeric(gsub("-99997", "0", .x)), .names = "num_{.col}"
    )) %>%
    mutate(
      female_share = num_vrouw / (num_man + num_vrouw),
      
      avg_age = (
        num_tot_15_jaar * 7.5 +
        num_x15_tot_25_jaar * 20 +
        num_x25_tot_45_jaar * 35 +
        num_x45_tot_65_jaar * 55 +
        num_x65_jaar_en_ouder * 75
      ) / (
        num_tot_15_jaar + num_x15_tot_25_jaar + num_x25_tot_45_jaar + num_x45_tot_65_jaar + num_x65_jaar_en_ouder
      ),
      
      avg_build_year = (
        num_voor_1945 * 1930 +
        num_x1945_tot_1965 * 1955 +
        num_x1965_tot_1975 * 1970 +
        num_x1975_tot_1985 * 1980 +
        num_x1985_tot_1995 * 1990 +
        num_x1995_tot_2005 * 2000 +
        num_x2005_tot_2015 * 2010 +
        num_x2015_en_later * 2020
      ) / (
        num_voor_1945 + num_x1945_tot_1965 + num_x1965_tot_1975 + num_x1975_tot_1985 +
        num_x1985_tot_1995 + num_x1995_tot_2005 + num_x2005_tot_2015 + num_x2015_en_later
      ),
      
      rental_share = (
        num_huurwoning + num_huurcoporatie
      ) / (
        num_koopwoning + num_huurwoning + num_huurcoporatie + num_niet_bewoond
      ),
      
      woz_corrected = num_woz_waarde_woning * 1000
    ) %>%
    select(postcode_6, female_share, avg_age, huishoudgrootte, avg_build_year, rental_share, woz_corrected)
}

cbs_pc6_clean <- process_cbs6_data(cbs_pc6)

cbs_pc4_clean <- process_cbs4_data(cbs_pc4)
  
#Add postcode_5 and postcode_4 to PC6 and PC5
cbs_pc6_clean <- cbs_pc6_clean %>%
  mutate(
    postcode_5 = str_sub(postcode_6, 1, 5),
    postcode_4 = str_sub(postcode_6, 1, 4)
  )

cbs_pc5_clean <- cbs_pc5_clean %>%
  mutate(
    postcode_4 = str_sub(postcode_5, 1, 4)
  )

pc6_joined <- cbs_pc6_clean %>%
  left_join(
    cbs_pc5_clean %>% select(-postcode_4),
    by = "postcode_5",
    suffix = c("_pc6", "_pc5")
  ) %>%
  left_join(cbs_pc4_clean, by = "postcode_4")

# Create fallback variables
fallback <- pc6_joined %>%
  mutate(
    female_share = coalesce(female_share_pc6, female_share_pc5, female_share),
    
    avg_age = coalesce(avg_age_pc6, avg_age_pc5, avg_age),
    
    huishoudgrootte = coalesce(
      na_if(as.numeric(huishoudgrootte), -99997),
      na_if(as.numeric(huishoudgrootte_pc5), -99997),
      na_if(as.numeric(huishoudgrootte), -99997)
    ),
    
    avg_build_year = coalesce(avg_build_year_pc6, avg_build_year_pc5, avg_build_year),
    
    rental_share = coalesce(rental_share_pc6, rental_share_pc5, rental_share),
    
    woz_corrected = coalesce(
      na_if(woz_corrected_pc6, 0),
      na_if(woz_corrected_pc5, 0),
      na_if(woz_corrected, 0)
    ),
    
    urban = urban
  ) %>%
  select(
    postcode_6,postcode_5,postcode_4, female_share, avg_age, huishoudgrootte,
    avg_build_year, rental_share, woz_corrected, urban
  ) 

# Load the 3rd sheet ("Tabel 1") starting after the first 5 rows

  "/Users/jeroen/Downloads/Datasegmentation for Jeroen/150911-Gemiddeld-besteedbaar-huishoudinkomen-per-postcode-mw.xls",
  sheet = "Tabel 1",
  skip = 9
)

income_raw<- income_raw[-1,-c(2:3)]

income_raw<-income_raw %>% rename(postcode_4=`Postcode 4-digit`,income_eur = `...4` ) %>% mutate(
    income_eur = na_if(income_eur, "."),
    income_eur = as.numeric(income_eur),
    income_z = (income_eur - 34500) / sd(income_eur, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
income_raw$postcode_4 <- as.character(income_raw$postcode_4)
  
# Join income_z into fallback dataframe using postcode_4
fallback <- fallback %>%
  left_join(income_raw %>% select(postcode_4, income_z), by = "postcode_4")
```

```{r}
#Read in new address list - Since the REL address list is confidential, I'll create a mock dataset for testing
#This should be updated to whatever addresses you require and thus different data cleaning steps may be required

# Create a mock address dataset using some BAG IDs from our downloaded data
set.seed(123)
bag_sample <- bag_data %>% 
  slice_sample(n = 50) %>%  # Take 50 random buildings
  select(bag_id)

# Create mock addresses with postcodes that exist in our CBS data
addresses_clean <- data.frame(
  `Nummeraanduiding (Bag ID)` = bag_sample$bag_id,
  Postcode = c("1421AA", "1421AB", "1421AC", "1421AD", "1421AE", 
               rep(c("1000AA", "1001AA", "1002AA", "1003AA", "1004AA"), 9)),
  Huisnummer = sample(1:200, 50),
  Straatnaam = "Test Street"
) %>%
  mutate(
    Postcode = as.character(Postcode),
    Huisnummer = as.character(Huisnummer)
  )

print("Created mock address dataset for testing:")
head(addresses_clean)
```

```{r}
#assemble new dataset 
# First, clean column name to make things easier
addresses_clean <- addresses_clean %>%
  rename(bag_id = `Nummeraanduiding (Bag ID)`)

# Now join BAG data and fallback postcode-level variables
test_dataset <- addresses_clean %>%
  left_join(
    bag_data %>%
      select(bag_id, oppervlakte_m2, year_built_cat),
    by = c("bag_id" = "bag_id")
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    fallback %>%
      select(postcode_6, female_share, avg_age, huishoudgrootte, rental_share, urban, income_z),
    by = c("Postcode" = "postcode_6")
  )

test_dataset <- test_dataset %>%
  rename(
    female        = female_share,
    age           = avg_age,
    members       = huishoudgrootte,
    year_built    = year_built_cat,
    rental        = rental_share,
    nettohh_z     = income_z,
    square_meters = oppervlakte_m2
  )

```

```{r} 
# Predict persona class probabilities
test_predictions <- predict(final_rf_model, data = test_dataset, type = "response")

# Add predictions to test_dataset
test_dataset$predicted_persona <- test_predictions$predictions

# For probabilities (optional)
test_probs <- predict(final_rf_model, data = test_dataset, type = "response", predict.all = FALSE)$predictions

# Add class probabilities
test_dataset <- bind_cols(test_dataset, as.data.frame(test_probs))

table(test_dataset$predicted_persona)

ggplot(test_dataset, aes(x = predicted_persona)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Predicted persona distribution", x = "Persona", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

#Test data set now contains predicted personas for each of the new addresses that we have been given in test_dataset$predicted_persona
```
